clue.text: 18th birthday do for Meg F — O can I go?

indicators.note: to do for something is to ruin or wreck it, so the letters that follow are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A teenager called Meg asks whether she may go to an 18th birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do for' signals the anagram: the letters of MEG F O CAN I GO, eleven in all, are rearranged. The odd 'F — O' makes the surface look like a garbled note, which is the clue that letters are being supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching eighteen is the traditional point of legal adulthood in Britain, celebrated as reaching majority.

clue.text: Reckon soft cheese (slightly misspelt) part of gesture for self-catering opportunities

parts.note: to reckon is to count or calculate

indicators.note: a small spelling slip swaps one letter of the cheese's name for another

parts.note: ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese

indicators.note: only the opening stretch of the word gesture is used here

explanation.surface: Someone works out cheese costs and gestures while planning holiday lets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly misspelt' turns RICOTTA into RYCOTTA by putting Y for I; 'part of' takes GES from the start of 'gesture'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural cottages rented out for holidays, where guests cook for themselves, are classic self-catering lets.

clue.text: Cereal I found in labyrinth

indicators.note: the letter I is discovered sitting inside the word for the labyrinth

parts.note: a labyrinth is a maze

explanation.surface: A lone cereal grain turns up in the middle of a maze.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, also called corn, is a cereal crop grown for its grain.

clue.text: Capital for Pole, first class, with tailless bird

parts.note: N stands for the North Pole
A1 is the old label for first class, written here as AI

indicators.note: without its tail means the last letter of the bird is cut off

parts.note: the robin is a common garden bird

explanation.surface: A Polish traveller flies first class to a capital with a bird missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: AI, from 'A1' (first class, originally Lloyd's register of ships), is a crossword staple; 'tailless' trims ROBIN to ROBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Base of rig — lubricate generously

definitions.meaning: an oil rig stands over a drilled well, its foundation in a sense
read as an instruction: apply oil, and do it well

explanation.definitionFit: A drilled shaft for petroleum sits under the rig, and 'oil well' also reads as a command to oil thoroughly.

clue.text: Pastoral connected with covered row of shops?

definitions.meaning: idyllically rural, like the ancient Greek region of shepherds

definitions.text: connected with covered row of shops?
definitions.meaning: an adjective made jokily from a shopping arcade, as if belonging to it

explanation.definitionFit: Arcadia was the idealised rustic land of poets, so its adjective means rural; the second sense is a punning coinage from arcade.

clue.text: Science — a little of it with a lot coming up — after vote for corporal punishment?

indicators.note: the reversed pieces follow the vote and the punishment

parts.note: to vote for someone is to elect them
the rod was used for beating

indicators.note: in a down clue each piece is read upwards, letters in reverse order

parts.note: it refers back to science, and a little of the word is SCI, its short form
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A scientist wonders whether voting for caning counts as a branch of science.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to 'Science', whose short form is a little of it; 'coming up' reads that and 'a lot' upwards together in this down clue, and 'after' places them behind the vote and the punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of moving electric charges and their interaction with magnetic fields is a branch of physics.

clue.text: Got the wrong way to the segregated area

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone took a wrong turning into a walled-off quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'the' is part of the anagram indicator 'the wrong way'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghetto is a district where a minority group is confined or concentrated apart from others.

clue.text: Girl at home with network

parts.note: in means at home
a grid is a network of lines

explanation.surface: A girl stays home on her computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingrid is a woman's first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: He escaped from the house to Ulster after mutiny

indicators.note: Ulster follows the mutiny

parts.note: HO is the usual abbreviation for house
UDI, a unilateral declaration of independence, is a rebellion against the ruling power
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A fugitive runs from a house to Ulster after a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: UDI recalls Rhodesia's 1965 break from Britain, a rebellion in effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the famous escapologist who got free of chains, locks and tanks.

clue.text: Hannibal's new desk

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal of Thomas Harris's novels; his surname is wanted

explanation.surface: A famous villain acquires a new piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hannibal' points to the Carthaginian general, but it is Hannibal Lecter whose surname gives LECTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a sloping reading desk, as used in churches and lecture halls.

clue.text: Hamlet, say, could guide tiller with toe

indicators.note: steering the letters of the following words directs them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor playing Hamlet steers a boat using a foot on the tiller.
explanation.walkthrough: The rudder image of tiller and guide disguises the anagram of TILLER and TOE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is the name role of Shakespeare's play, the part the play is named after.

clue.text: Put off portion of French potatoes

indicators.note: only part of the French phrase is kept, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: the French for potatoes is pommes de terre

explanation.surface: Someone is discouraged by a serving of French potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is not in the clue: translate 'French potatoes' to POMMES DE TERRE, then 'portion of' keeps DETER from the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage them from acting, to put them off.

clue.text: Stone horse with head missing and unknown addition

indicators.note: the first letter of the horse is removed

parts.note: a pony is a small horse
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A headless horse statue is given a mysterious extra piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head missing' turns PONY into ONY; 'addition' just joins the X on.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony, a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Dolls, I argue endlessly, should form band (not banned, they say)

indicators.note: the letters are to be shaped into something new
the last letter of the word argue is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone argues that their dolls should start a band that is not banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ARGUE to ARGU; DOLLS + I + ARGU are rearranged. The definition hints that the band's name sounds like 'girls allowed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls Aloud was a British pop girl group formed on a TV talent show in 2002.

clue.text: How hot could one get around the collar in formal dress?

parts.note: metal heated to its hottest glows white, as in white-hot
a tie is worn around the shirt collar

explanation.surface: A man in evening wear wonders how hot he could get under his collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot under the collar' suggests anger, a false trail: the first piece comes from the phrase white-hot, the hottest glow of heated metal.
explanation.definitionFit: White tie is the most formal evening dress code, with tailcoat and white bow tie.

clue.text: Science student Monbiot, losing a day, keeps nearly the whole shift

indicators.note: the trimmed name holds the next piece inside it
the named day is taken away from the journalist's name

parts.note: George Monbiot is a British environmental journalist
Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: the last letter of the garment is dropped

parts.note: a chemise is a loose dress or shift

explanation.surface: A science student named Monbiot loses a day but works almost an entire shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing a day' strips Monday's short form from the journalist's name; 'nearly the whole' drops the garment's last letter, and 'keeps' sets it inside the trimmed name.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of the chemistry of living things is studying a science.

clue.text: Large woman featuring two of any size

parts.note: large means big
Amy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A large woman wears clothes in a pair of any size.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is jokey: bigamy means having two spouses, whatever their size, a nod back to the 'large woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is marriage to a second spouse while still married to the first, so a pair of partners.

clue.text: Constituents of water in craze for shrub

indicators.note: the elements of water go inside the craze

parts.note: a mania is a craze
water is H2O, made of hydrogen and oxygen

explanation.surface: Ingredients of water are found in a fashion for a garden shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahonia is an evergreen shrub with holly-like leaves and yellow flowers.

clue.text: A wall painting not left in South Island depicting Japanese soldiers

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the abbreviations for south and island
not means the following letter is left out of the painting

parts.note: a mural is a painting on a wall

explanation.surface: A mural in the South Island of New Zealand shows Japanese warriors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not left' strips the left abbreviation from the painting; 'in' sets the result between the south and island abbreviations. 'depicting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan.

clue.text: Person of colour sounds terrible

indicators.note: the word is said out loud rather than read

parts.note: dire means terrible

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone's skin tone sounds awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person of colour' invites a reading about race, but it means someone who colours things.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyer works with colour, applying dyes to cloth or yarn.

clue.text: 8 inverted on horse

indicators.note: the two halves of the name are swapped over

parts.note: the answer to 8 down, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl turns upside down on her horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' here means the halves change places: ING and RID swap round.
explanation.definitionFit: To be riding is to be mounted on a horse.

clue.text: About time Billy was nobbled?

indicators.note: the goat goes around the time abbreviation

parts.note: a billy is a male goat

explanation.surface: It was high time a certain Billy was nobbled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time' reads as a phrase, but 'About' is the container indicator. 'was' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Got at means bribed or tampered with, just as a nobbled racehorse or juror is.

clue.text: Girl of superior sort breaks into collection of civil defenders

indicators.note: the girl and the class letter burst inside the collection

parts.note: a hoard is a stored collection
Meg is a girl's name
U is upper class, the superior social sort

explanation.surface: A posh girl breaks into a store of local defence volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' usage. The Home Guard was Britain's WWII volunteer defence force.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Guard was a part-time volunteer force formed to defend Britain at home, so civilian defenders.

clue.text: Cheese prepared for August do?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Cheese is laid on for a party in August.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges AUG (August) plus DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after the town.

clue.text: Not a stone turned by the big bang?

indicators.note: the whole phrase is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Something that is not a gemstone gets turned by the Big Bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses NOT A GEM as a whole. 'the big bang' suggests the origin of the universe, but it means a large nuclear explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: A megaton is an explosive force equal to a million tons of TNT, the measure of a huge blast.

clue.text: Gathering of alumni in the Indian Ocean

definitions.meaning: a meeting of old school or college classmates
a French island east of Madagascar

explanation.definitionFit: Former students meet at a get-together, and Réunion is an island department of France in the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Woman with grandmother gains result from goings-on

parts.note: she refers to a woman
nan is an informal word for a grandmother

indicators.note: the letters of the word gains are what results when rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman and her grandmother profit from some mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result' rearranges GAINS into IGANS; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shenanigans are mischievous or underhand goings-on.
